Akurateco Integrates with viaSocket to Automate Payment Operations Without Code
summary:
Akurateco, a white-label payment software vendor, has launched an integration with viaSocket, a no-code workflow automation platform that connects more than 2,300 business applications. The integration went live and lets teams run routine payment operations in Akurateco automatically, based on what happens in the other tools they use.
Five Akurateco actions are available in viaSocket: creating a checkout link, checking a transaction status by payment ID, capturing an authorized payment, refunding a payment in full or in part, and voiding a payment before settlement. Any of them can be added as a step in an automated workflow that starts in another app or runs on a schedule.
In practice, this replaces tasks that staff currently do by hand, switching between systems:
Checkout links: when a deal is marked as won in HubSpot or a new invoice row is added in Google Sheets, a checkout link is created in Akurateco and emailed to the customer automatically.
Refunds: when a support agent approves a refund in Zendesk, the refund is submitted in Akurateco, and the customer gets a confirmation.
Transaction checks: payment statuses are checked on a schedule and logged to Google Sheets, with a Slack alert sent when a payment is declined or stays pending.
Captures: when an order is marked as shipped in the merchant's order management system, such as Airtable or Salesforce, the authorized payment is captured in Akurateco without anyone opening the payment dashboard.
“Our clients spend time on steps that don’t require a decision, such as copying an order amount to create a payment link or looking up a transaction status for a support ticket,” said Andrew Riabchuk, Founder and CTO at Akurateco. “With viaSocket, those steps run automatically, and the team steps in only where a decision is needed.”
“We’re excited to partner with Akurateco to help businesses connect their payment infrastructure with the tools they use every day. With viaSocket’s AI-powered automation, businesses can connect Akurateco with their CRMs and other 2300+ applications to automate payment-related workflows, reduce manual work, and build more efficient processes with just a single prompt ”, said Divyansh Jain, Product and Growth at viaSocket.
How to get started
The integration is listed as “Akurateco” on the viaSocket marketplace. It is available to merchants whose payment provider runs on Akurateco’s platform, with no additional setup required on the provider’s side. The merchant requests three details from their provider: a merchant key, a password and an endpoint URL. They then sign up for a viaSocket account (a free plan is available), create a new workflow, select Akurateco as an action step and enter those details. No development work is required.

Acorns Acquires Frich, Expanding Its Financial Education Community
summary:
Acorns, the financial wellness company helping everyday Americans grow their money, today announced the acquisition of Frich, a community where young Americans learn about money from each other. Frich co-founders Katrin Kaurov and Aleksandra Medina join Acorns as Co-Leads of Education & Community.
The deal reflects Acorns’ broader goal of giving everyday Americans a real chance to grow their money. The acquisition brings Acorns a community of 1.6 million people and an organic creator network producing financial education content, extending the company's approach to reaching new investors through creator-led education.
Many people avoid investing because they feel like it's a club they don't belong to, and they assume everyone else understands it and they don't. That feeling often forms years before someone opens an investing app. This acquisition meets people in the peer conversations where they're already shaping their money habits. It also continues a pattern for Acorns: bring in strong fintech builders and let them build.
“Investing is intimidating,” said Noah Kerner, CEO of Acorns. “Doing it with others can help people get past that. Katrin and Aleksandra helped a lot of people say ‘I don't know’ out loud, and that's a good place to start. We keep betting on builders like them.”
Kaurov and Medina founded Frich in 2021 to address a gap in financial education for young adults. The company was built around the premise that people learn how to manage money from each other, through real, diverse stories from people like them, shared in group chats, comment sections and creator videos, rather than from spreadsheets or formal instruction. Along with its active community and organic creator network, Frich also developed a peer-benchmarking feature that lets members compare their financial habits with their peers’, answering a question many young Americans ask: is my situation typical?
“We spent five years getting people to talk openly about money,” said Katrin Kaurov, co-founder of Frich. “Acorns is the natural next step, because it lets us pair that conversation with investing and saving.”
“Money feels like culture when it's honest, relatable, and social,” added Aleksandra Medina, co-founder of Frich. "That's what we built at Frich. It's what we get to keep building at Acorns.”
Acorns has spent more than a decade building products for financial wellness across life stages, including offerings for kids, teens, young adults, and families. The Frich acquisition adds an entry point built on peer conversation, reaching people where they are already talking about money, often before they have decided to invest. It also gives Acorns a way to start reaching specific communities more deeply, through the conversations those groups are already having with each other. 
Existing Frich community members will be welcomed to Acorns. Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed. Kaurov and Medina joined Acorns this month.

AI Rivals Human Advisers as Brits Seek Financial Help Without Judgement
summary:
Judgment, jargon, and embarrassment remain major barriers holding Brits back from taking control of their money, driving a shift towards AI assistants for money guidance.
When asked who they would feel most comfortable approaching with a financial question, 18% of Brits said an AI assistant, just marginally second to a traditional financial adviser (19%), as revealed in a study commissioned by smart money app Plum.
Social media, where ‘finfluencers’ are most prevalent, ranks lowest overall, with only 1% of respondents saying they would feel most comfortable turning to these platforms.

The study reveals that over half (53%) of Brits have avoided asking someone a question about money because they were worried it would make them sound financially inexperienced. The same percentage (53%) said they have pretended to understand a financial term or conversation, signalling a fear of appearing uninformed in front of others. 
In addition, more than two fifths (42%) said they would feel more confident asking questions on financial topics if they knew they were not going to be judged, with 38% saying anonymity would help. 
This lack of confidence is particularly acute when it comes to investing, with stocks and shares cited as the topics Brits feel least equipped to navigate (44%).
Commenting on the findings, Will Bryant, Director of Wealth Strategy at Plum, said: 
“It’s easy to see why people are using AI to manage their finances. Money can feel like a difficult topic, especially as there’s often a sense that you’re supposed to know all the answers. Being able to ask questions privately, without worrying about what someone else might think, removes some of those barriers. 
“But knowing which sources to trust is paramount to keeping your money safe. Mainstream LLMs are not designed specifically to help you with your personal finances and lack the context, data security and financial tools that you can find on a specially designed service like Plum Plan."
“Technology can be a powerful tool to help build financial confidence, but only when the right tools are used thoughtfully.”
Plum Plan is an AI-powered tool in the Plum app that can suggest financial plans and gives details on the best financial products based on customers’ goals. Plum then uses automations to deposit money into their chosen products, including ISAs, easy access accounts and more.
Plum Plan is designed by financial experts, so customers can be sure they are receiving the best possible information. Plum is aiming to offer Targeted Support, regulated by the FCA, in the near future.

Deutsche Bank Deploys Farsight On-Premise Across Investment Banking and Capital Markets in Europe and the Americas
summary:
Farsight, the platform helping global financial services firms become AI-native, today announced its partnership with Deutsche Bank. Deutsche Bank has deployed Farsight at present across Investment Banking & Capital Markets teams in Europe and North America, bringing specialized AI directly into critical banking workflows while keeping sensitive data, proprietary knowledge and workflow activity within the bank’s own technology environment.
The on-premise deployment enables Deutsche Bank teams to apply AI to internal data and workflows while maintaining greater control over how that information is accessed and used. Farsight can incorporate the bank’s prior work, internal standards and proprietary data into workflows tailored to how individual teams operate, including their preferred formats, processes and standards. Bankers can then generate and refine materials through an automated chat experience that incorporates context and feedback over time.
“Our teams have very specific standards for what goes in front of a client, and those standards vary from group to group,” said George Tierney, Managing Director, Global Chief Operating Officer for M&A at Deutsche Bank. “Farsight gives our teams a way to apply AI to their own workflows and materials while operating within Deutsche Bank’s technology environment. That combination of control and customization is critical to making AI work in a global, regulated enterprise like Deutsche Bank.”
Financial institutions are increasingly moving AI beyond standalone experimentation and general-purpose assistants to specialized workflows. For regulated firms, this shift depends on access to data, much of which is sensitive. Running Farsight within the bank's infrastructure allows the platform to put that data to work where it can have the greatest impact, while financial institutions maintain control over the data.
“Banks have spent decades building proprietary data, workflows and judgment that shape how their teams work,” said Samir Dutta, Co-Founder and CEO of Farsight. “Running Farsight within a bank’s own infrastructure allows that knowledge to remain inside the institution while becoming part of how teams use AI. By incorporating banker feedback, Farsight can help AI reflect how a bank approaches client work rather than relying solely on general-purpose outputs.”
The Deutsche Bank deployment builds on Farsight’s growing presence across financial services, with the platform supporting teams at some of the world’s largest financial institutions.

IMF and World Bank Group Release the ‘Bangkok Blueprint’ to Combat Cyber-Enabled Fraud in Digital Finance
summary:
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank Group (WBG) Managements today released the Bangkok Blueprint, a high-level framework developed in coordination with the Bank of Thailand that aims to help countries prevent, detect, and address the growing threat of cyber-enabled fraud in digital financial services.
Digital finance has expanded access, innovation, and efficiency, but it has also enabled fraud to occur at greater speed, scale, and sophistication. Cyber-enabled fraud is increasingly linked to transnational organized crime and is ranked by INTERPOL as among the most threatening crimes globally, alongside drug trafficking and money laundering.
“Cyber-enabled fraud has become a global challenge that no country or institution can tackle alone. The Bangkok Blueprint reflects our shared commitment to strengthen cooperation, build trust, and promote a safe and inclusive digital financial future for all,” said Vitai Ratanakorn Governor of the Bank of Thailand. 
Released during the 2026 IMF–WBG Annual Meetings in partnership with the Thai authorities, the Blueprint sets out 12 key considerations to help countries identify vulnerabilities and develop comprehensive, coordinated responses. By promoting a more coherent approach across sectors and jurisdictions, the Blueprint sees to strengthen trust in digital financial services and support their continued contribution to growth and inclusion.
“Trust is the foundation of every financial system. As digital finance expands, countries must work together to combat cyber-enabled fraud and preserve confidence in the technologies that support growth and inclusion,” said Kristalina Georgieva, the Managing Director of the IMF.
The Bangkok Blueprint is organized around five pillars: establishing strategic and legal foundations; strengthening the fraud-mitigation life cycle; leveraging existing risk-mitigation and enforcement frameworks; expanding domestic and cross-border cooperation; and promoting consumer protection and resilience.
“Digital financial services can be a powerful driver of economic opportunity, jobs, and financial inclusion in developing economies. Strengthening protection against fraud is essential to ensuring that people can use these services with confidence and fully benefit from the opportunities they create,” said Anshula Kant, Managing Director and World Bank Group Chief Financial Officer.
Recognizing that fraud schemes often involve social media, digital platforms, e-commerce, and telecommunications networks, the Blueprint emphasizes clear accountability and timely cooperation across the public and private sectors, both domestically and across borders. It encourages countries to tailor the 12 considerations to their legal, institutional, and market conditions.
“As digital finance becomes increasingly interconnected, our response to fraud must be equally connected. The Bangkok Blueprint provides a foundation for stronger cooperation and collective action to protect citizens and strengthen trust in the digital economy,” said Ekniti Nitithanprapas, Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister of Thailand.
By fostering a safer and more trusted financial ecosystem, the Blueprint seeks to help countries harness the full potential of digital finance to expand opportunity, inclusion and sustainable growth.

StraitsX Partners with Visa to Expand Its Reach to Over 100 Markets Globally Through Stablecoin-Backed Card Programs
summary:
StraitsX, the stablecoin-native settlement layer powering global finance, today announced that it is partnering with Visa, the world’s leader in digital payments to expand its card issuing capabilities globally to more than 100 markets. 
The milestone extends StraitsX’s card issuing infrastructure beyond its established footprint in Asia, enabling the company to support eligible card issuance programs globally and is subject to applicable regulatory, compliance and Visa requirements. This expanded capability is designed for fintechs, Digital Payment Token (DPT) service providers, wallets, and other businesses looking to build card programs that connect stablecoin balances and digital asset payment flows with Visa’s global acceptance network.
From rapid growth in Asia to global card issuing
The expansion follows a period of significant growth for StraitsX’s card issuing business in Asia. StraitsX reached an annualised card GTV of more than US$6 billion across its stablecoin-backed card programs.
With the partnership with Visa, StraitsX can now extend the infrastructure and experience behind this growth to businesses building card programs across global markets.
“Stablecoin-backed cards have become one of the clearest examples of how stablecoins can move beyond settlement and into everyday payments,” said Tianwei Liu, CEO and Co-Founder of StraitsX. “We have seen significant growth in this use case across Asia. Expanding our issuing capabilities globally allows us to bring the same infrastructure to businesses looking to build and scale card programs across markets.”

Connecting stablecoins with global card acceptance
Stablecoin-backed cards provide a practical bridge between digital value and existing payment networks, allowing businesses to extend the utility of stablecoins without requiring merchants or consumers to adopt an entirely new payment experience.
StraitsX enables fintechs, DPT service providers and wallets to build card programs where stablecoins can support the underlying funding and settlement flow, while cardholders continue to transact through familiar Visa credentials and its global acceptance network.
For businesses operating across multiple markets, this brings together stablecoin-native infrastructure and global card issuing capabilities through a single infrastructure partner.
This collaboration will also take into account the continuously evolving nature of money-laundering and terrorism financing typologies and ensure that such risks arising from this integration are properly mitigated.
“At Visa, we are focused on bringing the benefits of new payment technologies into the global financial system in a way that is secure, scalable and trusted,” said Rubail Birwadker, Global Head of Growth Products & Partnerships, Visa. Working closely with our partner, StraitsX, we are unlocking more ways to use stablecoins for real-world payment flows, while connecting them to the reach and reliability of Visa’s global network.”

Building global payment infrastructure on stablecoin rails
The expansion of StraitsX’s card issuing capabilities is part of a broader strategy to connect stablecoins with the financial and payment infrastructure businesses already use today.
Beyond card issuing, StraitsX provides stablecoin-native infrastructure for payments and settlement, enabling businesses to move and use digital value across markets. As new forms of commerce emerge, including payments initiated by AI agents, StraitsX is building the infrastructure to connect these new payment flows with existing financial networks.
By expanding its Visa card issuing capabilities globally, StraitsX is extending this infrastructure to businesses looking to launch and scale stablecoin-backed card programs across markets.

Nuvei Secures License to Offer Local Payment Acceptance in South Africa
summary:
Nuvei, the global fintech building the infrastructure for every payment, everywhere, today announced that it has secured authorization from the Payments Association of South Africa (PASA) to offer local merchant payment services in South Africa, expanding its ability to support global brands and local businesses through its global payments platform.
The authorization advances Nuvei's Every Payment Everywhere strategy, extending its presence within domestic payment ecosystems to help businesses optimize payment performance in every market they operate. By adding South Africa to its network, Nuvei is extending its local acquiring and payment acceptance infrastructure, transaction data, and operational controls to another major market, accessible through a single global platform.
Phil Fayer, Chair and CEO of Nuvei, said: ”Commerce is global, but payment performance is local. Our expansion into South Africa is another step towards giving businesses access to locally optimized payment capabilities at global scale. South Africa is one of Africa's most important digital commerce markets, and strengthening our presence here creates new opportunities for international businesses entering the region and South African companies expanding globally.”
A growing digital commerce market
South Africa’s B2C ecommerce market grew by an estimated 9.9% in 2025 to reach $8.48 billion, according to research published by PayNXT360. The market is forecast to expand at a compound annual growth rate of 8.3% through 2029, reaching approximately $11.66 billion. This continued growth is increasing the importance of locally optimized payment performance for businesses competing in the market.
Bringing global brands closer to the local market
Processing transactions domestically can improve authorization rates compared with cross-border acquiring, reduce processing costs, and give businesses more complete visibility into transaction performance. Direct access to local transaction data also supports more precise fraud management and enables businesses to identify and address sources of payment friction more effectively.
Global brands entering South Africa will be able to access these capabilities through the same Nuvei integration they use across other markets. Businesses already serving South African consumers cross-border will be able to establish a more locally optimized payments operation without adding a separate gateway, acquiring relationship, and reporting environment. That gives them room to adapt the checkout experience to local expectations while managing authorization, fraud prevention, reconciliation, and reporting through one platform.

title: Convera Appoints Four Senior Leaders to Accelerate Its Global Money Movement Platform
summary:
Convera, a global leader in commercial payments, today announced four senior leadership appointments: Mike Cahill as EVP and Chief Operating Officer; Jon Southall as SVP and Chief Technology Officer; Tui Allen as SVP and Chief Product Officer; and Chris Steinig as Chief Information Officer. Together, they bring extensive experience in building and scaling global payments, product, technology and operational platforms. They will lead the execution of Convera’s roadmap for an integrated global money movement platform that combines cross-border payments, FX risk management and multi-currency capabilities for businesses.
Convera’s strategy is built on a simple premise: as agentic commerce emerges and volatility persists, businesses operating across borders need integrated solutions. They need to send, receive and hold money in the currencies they trade in, manage FX exposure at the point of payment, and route transactions across the most appropriate payment rail for speed, cost and visibility.
“Businesses don’t just need faster or less expensive cross-border payments. They need to know where their money is, what it is worth and how to protect it as it moves,” said Patrick Gauthier, Group CEO at Convera. “That is the opportunity in front of Convera. Our global reach, FX expertise, regulatory depth and customer relationships enable us to solve that problem in a way few providers can. Mike, Jon, Tui and Chris are proven leaders with the experience, judgement and execution discipline to help us deliver for customers. Each brings a distinct perspective, and together they give us the leadership depth to advance our roadmap for integrated cross-border money movement.”
Advancing customer-led execution
Mike Cahill has been appointed EVP and Chief Operating Officer, leading Convera’s combined Product, Technology and Operations organization. Since joining Convera in June 2026 as Interim Chief Product and Technology Officer, he has focused on bringing these functions together to deliver a more connected customer experience. Cahill has scaled mission-critical financial platforms and led complex transformations at Early Warning Services, the company behind Zelle, as well as at PayPal, Boku and American Express.
Jon Southall joins as SVP and Chief Technology Officer from PayPal, where he managed the Large Enterprise Platform, which supports more than $1.5 trillion in annual transaction volume. He has also built scaled payment platforms at Boku and Braintree. His experience in high-volume infrastructure will help Convera deliver faster, more reliable and more visible money movement for customers.
Tui Allen joins as SVP and Chief Product Officer from Ticketmaster/Live Nation, where she helped modernize product experiences at scale. She previously built new solutions at Shopify. Allen brings experience translating complex customer needs into scalable products that are easier to use, integrate and adopt.
Chris Steinig has been appointed Chief Information Officer after leading Convera’s technology operations. A 25-year veteran of the company, he brings deep knowledge of Convera’s systems, infrastructure and operating environment. Steinig will connect platform modernization, enterprise technology and operational resilience to help ensure the company delivers its roadmap with the reliability and control customers expect.

Starling Becomes First Bank to Train AI Model on UK Sovereign Cloud
summary:
Starling is building a transactional foundation model (TFM) with support from NVIDIA that will be the first banking model to be trained and hosted within a UK sovereign cloud.* Working with UK cloud provider Civo, Starling is supercharging its ability to design tools for customers while also supporting the growth of UK cloud capability.
The model will be trained on proprietary Starling data from over 15 billion anonymised transactions to give the bank deeper insight into the needs and behaviours of its customers. In time, it will form a single intelligence layer - ‘Starling Intelligence’ - that elevates the bank’s AI capabilities and enables it to build entirely new experiences.
“We’ve made huge strides with our proprietary AI tools, launching the UK’s first agentic AI financial assistant and rolling out new features every week. Now we want to connect these tools with a single intelligence layer that’s trained entirely on the specific needs of our customers,” said Harriet Rees, Group CIO at Starling and a UK Government AI Champion for Financial Services. “We also want to take a leadership role in the development of home-grown cloud infrastructure, which is essential to European companies’ ability to diversify their suppliers and reduce concentration risk.” 
By training its TFM on Civo’s UK cloud, Starling is following recommendations made in the UK Government’s Financial Services AI Adoption Plan, co-authored by Harriet Rees and published in July 2026. The plan flags a reliance on a small number of global AI and cloud providers and recommends that government and industry broaden their partnerships to improve optionality and systemic resilience.
“AI will only deliver lasting value for the UK economy if it’s built on secure, resilient, sovereign infrastructure,” said Mark Boost, CEO of Civo. “Starling is leading the financial sector by training and hosting its Transactional Foundation Model on a homegrown cloud. Pairing NVIDIA compute with Civo’s UK sovereign cloud shows that banks don’t have to trade performance or innovation for control of their data, or depend on a handful of global providers.”
The TFM will be developed with NVIDIA’s financial services team, using NVIDIA’s Transaction Foundation Model developer blueprint, including NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries for GPU-accelerated data processing and NVIDIA NeMo AutoModel for model training. 
Optimised for high-performance AI workloads, Civo’s sovereign infrastructure, from NVIDIA Hopper GPUs to upcoming Vera Rubin deployments, provides the low-latency compute and advanced liquid cooling essential for real-time reasoning, autonomous systems, and agentic AI. It will create a reusable intelligence layer capable of identifying patterns in anonymised transaction data and supporting multiple applications.
“Banks are at the forefront of turning massive amounts of data into timely, personalised insights while also protecting customers from fraud,” said Aser Blanco, Global Head of Banking at NVIDIA. “By combining NVIDIA’s accelerated computing and software for data processing and model training with Civo’s UK sovereign cloud, Starling can deliver exceptional customer experiences while maintaining control of its customers’ data.”
Starling intends to put its TFM into production in early 2027, initially to improve existing AI services around fraud detection and then to augment Starling Assistant, the UK’s first agentic AI financial assistant. The Starling Intelligence layer will enable Starling Assistant to provide more personalised experiences, such as proactively serving bespoke budgeting guidance.
